evals.prompt: Review this PR for security issues before I merge: https://github.com/acme/rails-app/pull/482
evals.expected_output: PR mode. Reads the diff via GitHub MCP, runs static + inspection scoped to the change, posts inline comments tagged with OWASP 2025 category + severity + fix, and a summary review that requests changes only if Critical/High exist. Does not gate on pre-existing issues the PR didn't introduce.

evals.prompt: Audit this Rails app for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities and give me a report.
evals.expected_output: Repo mode. Runs Brakeman + bundler-audit, sweeps all ten categories by inspection, confirms tool leads in code, and writes owasp-review-<date>.md with findings sorted by severity, category rollup, and recommended manual checks.

evals.prompt: Is this controller safe? It does `@order = Order.find(params[:id])` then renders it as JSON for the current user.
evals.expected_output: Identifies A01 Broken Access Control / IDOR: unscoped find lets any authenticated user read others' orders. Assigns Critical/High, explains the attack, and gives the scoped-find fix (current_user.orders.find). Stays read-only.

evals.prompt: We just added a Stripe webhook endpoint and a background job that fetches a user-supplied image URL. Any security concerns?
evals.expected_output: Flags A08 (webhook signature verification — must verify Stripe HMAC before acting) and A01 SSRF (user-supplied URL fetch needs host allow-listing). Both tool-blind, found by reasoning. Gives concrete Rails remediations.
